title: Word Break Segmentation
statement: A label printer jams whenever it hits a space, so product codes are printed as one unbroken string. Given a string s and a list words of approved code fragments, decide whether s can be split into a sequence of fragments taken from words, concatenated with nothing in between. Each fragment may be reused any number of times, and the split must consume s exactly (no leftover characters). Return True if such a split exists, else False. An empty s counts as trivially splittable (a sequence of zero fragments), so return True for it.
hints: Greedily grabbing the longest (or first) matching fragment can strand you: taking 'aaa' from 'aaab' leaves an unmatchable 'b'. What lets you consider every possible split point instead of committing to one?

Define dp[i] = True when the prefix of s of length i can be split into fragments. dp[0] is True (empty prefix), and dp[i] is True if any earlier reachable prefix dp[j] extends to i via a fragment: s[j:i] in the word set.
Build dp of size len(s)+1 with dp[0]=True. For each i from 1 to len(s), scan j from 0 to i-1; if dp[j] and s[j:i] is in the fragment set, set dp[i]=True and break. Answer is dp[len(s)].
